cases.question: Why did checkout requests time out after release R42?

sources.description: Deployment, routing, and rollback records for R41 and R42
Correlated request traces and pool telemetry for the declared window

hypotheses.statement: R42 leaks database connections after cancelled checkout requests.
hypotheses.necessary_prediction: Pool occupancy and wait time rise on R42 before request timeouts.
hypotheses.disproof_criterion: R42 releases cancelled-request connections before any pool growth.

hypotheses.statement: The database service slowed all checkout instances.
hypotheses.necessary_prediction: Database execution latency rises on both R41 and R42.
hypotheses.disproof_criterion: Database execution latency remains stable on both releases.

tests.result: Correlated traces show cancelled R42 requests retain connections until pool exhaustion.
R41 controls retain normal pool occupancy and database execution latency.
An authorized isolated replay reproduces the leak on R42 but not R41.
Rolling back only R42 restores pool occupancy and checkout success.

evidence.observation: Connection retention begins before pool exhaustion and request timeouts only on R42.
Replay reproduces the timing and failure on R42 and does not reproduce it on R41.
Rollback from R42 to R41 restores pool occupancy and checkout success without a database change.

cases.question: Why did the daily order total double?

sources.description: Curated order table and source order ledger
Retained merge configuration and transformation code

hypotheses.statement: A retry duplicated records during ingestion.
hypotheses.necessary_prediction: A retained retry identifier or replay distinguishes retry output.

hypotheses.statement: A later merge step duplicated records.
hypotheses.necessary_prediction: Transformation lineage identifies duplicate emission after ingestion.

tests.result: The curated table contains duplicate order IDs with matching payloads.
The source ledger contains one row per duplicated order ID.
The retained merge configuration permits duplicate emission but contains no row-level lineage that distinguishes a retry from a later merge.

evidence.observation: Duplicate rows appear only after the source ledger and are identical at the compared fields.
The retained transformation can emit the observed duplicates through either active hypothesis.

gaps.description: No retained row-level lineage can distinguish retry output from later merge output.

cases.question: Did a cache initialization race return stale account permissions?

scope.affected: All requests that returned stale permissions in the captured incident window
scope.unaffected: Concurrency stress-test requests using the same cache path

sources.description: Complete request traces for every stale-permission response

hypotheses.statement: Concurrent cache initialization publishes an incomplete permission set.
hypotheses.necessary_prediction: A failing request reads the cache while initialization is incomplete.
hypotheses.disproof_criterion: Complete failing-request traces place every cache read after initialization.

tests.result: Complete traces cover every failing request and show cache initialization finished before each read.
A concurrency stress test reaches the suspected interleaving without returning stale permissions.

evidence.observation: Every captured failing request reads the cache after initialization completed.
The suspected interleaving does not produce stale permissions under stress.

cases.question: Why was an unapproved pricing rule released?

scope.affected: Pricing-rule release and approval records for the incident
scope.unaffected: Three comparable releases using the same manual transition

sources.description: Retained approval records and owner interviews

hypotheses.statement: The release workflow allowed the approval handoff to be skipped.
hypotheses.necessary_prediction: The manual transition can bypass the approval stage.

hypotheses.statement: An approver explicitly approved the rule outside the tracked workflow.
hypotheses.necessary_prediction: An external approval record or accountable witness confirms the decision.

tests.result: Workflow history shows the approval stage was bypassed through an allowed manual transition.
Three comparable releases used the same transition and also omitted the approval record.

evidence.observation: The allowed manual transition bypasses the approval stage and was used for the incident release.
No retained record or accountable witness confirms an external approval.

gaps.description: An external approval remains possible because the mailbox did not retain the relevant period.
